11. LEGAL STANDARDS
a. Review of Mpgi$tr*tL? lydgg's Report and Recommendation
A U.S. District Judge may refer certain types of pending matters to a U. S. Magistrate Judge
for a Report and Recommendation. 28 U.S.C. 636(b)(I)(B); Fed. R . Civ. P. 72(b)(1). Parties
may file written objections to an R&R within fourteen days of its issuance. 28 U.S.C.
636(b)(1)(C); Fed. R. Civ. P. 72(b)(2). An argument that has not been raised in front of the
magistrate judge is 'h10t entitled to a de novo review." Mills v. Turner, No. 15-13267-MLW, 2017
U.S. Dist. LEXIS 136887, at *3 (D. Mass. Aug. 25, 2017) (quoting Borden v. Sec'y 0fHea1t!1 &
Human Serys., 836 F. 2d 4, 6 (1st Cir. 1987)). Objections containing arguments or referring to
previously available evidence that were not raised before the magistrate judge are deemed waived.
836 F.2d at 6 (explaining that a party objecting to a report and recommendation is 'flot
entitled to a de novo review of an argument never raised" before the magistrate)•see

to a Magistrate Judge for a recommended disposition, the District Judge must "determine de novo
any part of the magistrate judge's disposition that has been properly objected to." Fed. R. Civ. P.
72(b)(3). When conducting a de novo review, the U .S. District Judge "may accept, reject, or modify
the recommended disposition; receive further evidence; or return the matter to the magistrate judge
with instructions." Fed. R. Civ. P U.S.C. "Where objections to an
R&R are repetitive of the arguments already made to the magistrate judge, a de novo review is
unwarranted." Rojas-Busqaglia v: Taburno-Vasarely, 39 F. Supp. 3d 208, 212 n.l (D.P.R. 2014)
(citing Westernbank P.R. v. Kachkqr, No. 07-1606 (ADO, 2009 U.S. Dist. LEXIS 78726, at *25
(D.P.R. Sept. l, 2009)). "Instead, the report and recommendation is reviewed by the district judge

23-CV-12625-MRG, 2025 U.S. Dist. LEXIS 64359, at *9 n.6 (D. Mass. Mar. 31, 2025) ("Indeed,
the clear error standard applies to such improper objections" (citations omitted)).
b. Motion to Dismiss for Lack of Subiect Matter Jurisdiction
"Jurisdiction is the cornerstone of every federal court action." Woo v. Spackman. 988 F.
3d 47, 53 (1st Cir. 2021). Therefore, when faced with a motion to dismiss under both and
12(b)(6), a district court "ordinarily decide[s] the 12(b)(1) motion first."
BTEA v. Sec'y of Labor, 62 F. 3d 37, 39 (1st Cir. 1995). The Court evaluates alleged facts in the
complaint "at face value" to determine whether they support subject-matter jurisdiction.
873 F. 3d 32, 35 (1st Cir. 2017). The plaintiff bears the burden to
establish that the federal court has subject-matter jurisdiction. Klimowicz v. Deutsqhe Bank Nat'l
Tr. Co., 907 F. 3d 61, 64 (1st Cir. 2018). "If the party fails to demonstrate a basis for jurisdiction,

conclusions or interpretations of law" or "[slubjective characterizations or conclusory descriptions
of a general scenario which could be dominated by unpleaded facts." Murphy v. United States, 45
F.3d 520, 522 (1st Cir. 1995), cert. dgnigd, 515 U.S. 1144 (1995). In evaluating whether the party
has met its burden of proof, the court "may consider extrinsic materials and, to the extent it engages
in jurisdictional factfinding, is free to test the truthfulness of the plaintiffs allegations."
Image Techs.. Inc. v. United States, 221 F.3d 34, 37 (1st Cir. 2000) (citing Mortensen Firs! Fed.
say & Loan Ass'n, 594 F.2d 884, 890-91 (3rd Cir. 1977)). Rooker-Fe1dmap doctrine is
jurisdictional in nature; if a case is dismissed because the Rooker-FeIdman doctrine applies, it
means the court has no subject-matter jurisdiction to hear the case." Mills v. Harmon Law Offices:

[ECF No. 139 at 2]. This objection ßflects a fundamental misunderstanding of the statutory
framework governing reports and recommendations and is without merit I Under 28 U.S.C.

the Court warns Plaintiff that generative AI does not necessarily generate accurate findings of law,
can create incorrect or made-up citations, and should not be relied upon without review as a source

636(b)(I)(B) ("5 636"), a district judge may refer dispositive matters, including motions to
dismiss, to a magistrate judge for a report and recommendation, regardless of the parties' consent
ld.; see also Fed. R. Civ. P. 72(b)(I) (discussing magistrates judges' ability to issue R&R's "without
the parties consenß' (emphasis added)). Here, Judge Hennessy did not enter a final order disposing
of Plaintiff's claims independently; consistent with 636(b), Judge Hennessy issued an R&R
pertaining to Plaintiff's claims, which has no operative effect unless and until adopted by the
District Court. The District Judge's initials in the case caption or docket designation merely reflect
the administrative assignment of the case. The presence of thc District Judge's initials does not
limit the judge's statutory authority to matters to a magistrate judge, nor does it preclude a
magistrate judge from issuing a report and recommendation. The absence of Plaintiff's consent is
therefore legally irrelevant to the R&R process. See Cugini Ventetuolq, 781 F.Supp. 107, 108
n. I (D.R.I. 1992) (plaintiff's lack of consent for magistrate jurisdiction was of "no consequence").
Accordingly, Plaintiff's objection based on the absence of consent or lack of authority is overruled.
b. Objection to the R&R's Rulings on Plaintiff's Motion under Fed. R. Civ. P.
In the first and second R&Rs [ECF Nos. 116, 1181, Judge Hennessy denied Plaintiff's
motion for emergency relief from a judgment under Fed. R. Civ. P. 60(b)(4). [ECF No. 116 at 2-
31. Plaintiff sought to render void a prior R&R, [ECF No. 45 at 4—6], that denied injunctive relief
of sound legal arguments. For instance, Plaintiff cites to 28 U.S.C. 636(b)(l)(B) as supporting
authority for the assertion that ' 'a magistrate may recommend but cannot strike pleadings absent
district-judge adoption," which is wholly unsupported by the language of the statute. On the
contrary, 28 U.S.C. 636(b)(l)(A) and Fed. R. Civ. P. 72 empower magistrate judges to rule on
non-dispositive motions, such as a motion to amend a complaint. 28 U.S.C. 636(b)(l)(A); Fed.
R. Civ. P. 72(a); Pagano v. Frank, 983 F. 2d 343, 346 (1st Cir. 1993). Additionally, Plaintiff states
that Judge Hennessy's R&R referenced two cases, Ankenbrandt v. Richards 504 U.S. 689 (1992)
and Seminole Tribe v. Florida, 517 U.S. 44 (1996) [ECF No. 139 at 6]; however, neither case is
cited in the R&Rs pending this Court. [Sgg ECF Nos. 116, 1361.

because Plaintiff had failed to show likelihood of success on the merits where the relief he sought

Upon de novo review, the Court finds that Judge Hennessy correctly stated the legal

for relief from a judgment on the basis that it is void pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 60(b)(4). As the
First Circuit has explained,
There are only two sets of circumstances in which a judgment is void (as opposed
to voidable). The first is when the rendering court lacked either subject matter
jurisdiction or jurisdiction over a defendant's person. The second is when the
rendering court's actions so far exceeded a proper exercise of judicial power that a
violation of the Due Process Clause results.
Carrasquillo-Serrano v. Municipalib' Cpnpyanas, 991 F.3d 32, 39 (1st Cir. 2021) (quoting
Credit Bank v. Ferrera-Goitia, 316 F.3d 62, 67 (1st Cir. 2003)). Applying this standard, Judge
Hennessy denied Plaintiff's motion because he did not argue in any prior motions that this Court
lacks jurisdiction over his claims or that this Court had exceeded the "proper exercise of judicial
power that a violation of the Due Process clause results." [ECF No. 116 at 2—3 (quoting
Carrasquillo-Serrano, 991 F.3d at 39)].
Plaintiff asserts that Judge Hennessy misapprehended his argument. [ECF No. 117 at 2-3]
Plaintiff concedes that he is not contending that Court lacked jurisdiction. [ld.] Plaintiff states,
"the Court's prior order was void because it rested upon and gave effect to state child-support
orders that were themselves entered without valid service, notice, or personal jurisdiction" and "[al
federal order that enforces or incorporates void state orders operates 'in a manner inconsistent with
due process,' and is void within the meaning of Fed. R. Civ. P. 60(b)(4)." Lat 21 As a
preliminary matter, because Plaintiff asserted a near identical argument in his prior filings, [seg

'Ille Supreme Court of the United States is the only federal court with jurisdiction to review
a state court judgment. 28 U.S.C. 1257; Exxon Mobil Corp. v. Saudi Basic Indus. Corp., 544

Instead, 'the proper forum for challenging an unlawful state court ruling is the United States
Supreme Court, on appeal of the highest state court's final judgment."

[ECFNo. 136 at IO—III. Plaintiff did not object to this portion of Judge Hennessy's analysis. [Seg

Plaintiff reiterates this argument in his Emergency Objection to the R&R, but this time

lnL, 485 U.S. 80 (1988), and Student Aid Funds. Inc. v. Espinosa. 559 U.S. 260 (2010).
[ECF No. 139 at 21. However, none of those cases address whether a federal district court has
subject matter jurisdiction over a challenge to a state court judgment. Whether the state court had
personal jurisdiction to issue a judgment, and whether the federal court has subject matter
jurisdiction to review or invalidate that judgment, are distinct inquiries. There is no authority
supporting Plaintiff's proposition that federal district courts have subject matter jurisdiction over
jurisdictionally defective state court judgments. To the contrary, even where a state court is alleged
to have violated constitutional limits on personal jurisdiction, federal district courts remain without
jurisdiction to declare such judgments void. Schmitt, 324 F.3d at 487 (Rooker-Feldman bars
consideration of whether state court lacked personal jurisdiction). The proper place to challenge
the validity of a state court judgment is in the state's highest appellate court, or the United States
Supreme Court. Payispn, 471 F.3d at 223.
Discerning no error in the Magistrate's analysis, the Court overrules Plaintiff's objection
to the application of the Rooker-Feldman doctrine.

stage. Because ajudgment entered without personal jurisdiction is void ab initio, these

Who is required to withhold income?
Page: 2
Date Filed: 04/29/2026

Massachusetts law requires that employers and all other payors of periodic income must withhold for
child support. In this policy, the term employer includes the following:
Employers (including businesses who hire contractors);
• DUA and other state's unemployment agencies;
• SSA;
• Insurers (e.g. WC insurers);
Payors of annuities;
Any other entity that makes payments to a person on a periodic (e.g. monthly, weekly) basis.
When must an employer begin withholding?
By law, the employer does not have to change its payroll cycle to accommodate the payment frequency
noted in a court order. The employer must begin withholding income on the first payment cycle that
occurs at least 3 days after receiving the IWO from DOR and must send the amount withheld to DOR
within 3 business days of when the income would have been paid to the parent.
How long is an employer required to withhold?
The employer must continue withholding until it receives a new IWO from DOR instructing the employer
to withhold $0.
Note: If the employer receives a copy of a court order terminating withholding, the employer
cannot rely on the order to stop withholding. The employer must send the order to DOR and
await instructions from DOR.
How does an employer send payments to DOR?
Employers with five or more employees with I WOs must send payments to DOR through Electronic
Funds Transfer (EFT). Employers with fewer than five employees may send a check, but may sign up for
EFT voluntarily.
What if DOR sends more than one IWO for the same parent?
Since IWOs are case-specific, DOR sends an employer a separate IWO for each case a parent has. If the
employer receives more than one IWO for the same parent, the employer sends the total withholding
amount due for all of the IWOs and DOR allocates the payments according to our distribution rules.
Who determines how much income should be withheld?
The employer must withhold the total amount indicated in the IWOs unless the total exceeds the
maximum an employer may withhold from a parent's wages.
What is the maximum amount an employer can withhold from a parent's wages?
The federal Consumer Credit Protection Act (CCPA) sets the maximum amount that an employer can
withhold from a parent's income. The employer, not DOR, is responsible for calculating the CCPA limits.
What are the CCPA limits for withholding child support?
The CCPA sets the following limits for child support withholding:
For a parent who is supporting other dependents:
• 50% if the amount owed is less than 12 weeks past due
• 55% if the amount owed is more than 12 weeks past due
For a parent who is not supporting other dependents:
• 60% if the amount owed is less than 12 weeks past due
• 65% if the amount owed is more than 12 weeks past due

A garnishment (also known in some states as a levy) is a legal order that allows a creditor to remove money from
your bank account(s) to satisfy a debt you owe. In other words, if you owe money to a creditor, the creditor can
obtain a court order directing your bank to take money out of your account(s) and turn it over to the creditor to pay
off your debt. The bank is legally obligated to comply with the terms of the court order.
